answer: A bond-backed identity market stops fake agents the way a copper mine stops freeloaders: every agent locks a refundable stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers prove it runs multiple identities. Like tending an orchard, the bond gains value only through honest seasons of work, so a cheap clone planted in the tundra of throwaway accounts starves — the attacker must fund each fake separately, and every proven fraud burns that stake instead of buying influence.
